headline: Medium risk: shared MCP/file surfaces create prompt-injection and data-leak pathways; OpenBB’s default API-driven workflows can amplify cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx ingests filesystem and MCP-adjacent events, while OpenBBTerminal uses MCP servers and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from ctx can reach OpenBB as trusted input. The pair lacks documented provenance filtering, so the interaction is not blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF ctx-observed content is forwarded into OpenBBTerminal prompts or MCP inputs without provenance tags
IF OpenBBTerminal parses ctx output as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a manual review step before passing ctx output into OpenBB inputs
Prefix all forwarded content with explicit data/instruction labels
Disable automatic ingestion of ctx logs into OpenBB workflows
Use separate workspaces for ctx and OpenBBTerminal
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware filtering between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and filesystem content; OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and can use MCP/REST APIs. A shared workspace or copied files could expose sensitive financial or operational data across the pair. The profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem or copied artifacts
IF ctx logs or graph data contain financial or licensed data later opened by OpenBBTerminal
mitigations: Keep ctx and OpenBBTerminal in separate directories
Avoid copying logs or graph exports between agents
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Restrict OpenBBTerminal API credentials to least privilege
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx supports multiple instances and writes to filesystem-related surfaces, but OpenBBTerminal cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read/consume behavior through shared MCP or files, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF ctx is configured to mutate shared files that OpenBBTerminal also reads
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize any shared-file updates manually
Make OpenBBTerminal read-only on shared artifacts
Use file locks for any common workspace
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx observes tool events and can shape context, while OpenBBTerminal’s connect-once-consume-everywhere workflow can treat upstream outputs as authoritative. If ctx emits incorrect summaries or instructions, OpenBBTerminal may propagate them into financial analysis or API-driven actions without a verification gate.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes ctx-generated summaries without independent validation
IF ctx output is used to drive downstream financial queries or reports
mitigations: Require source citations before OpenBBTerminal acts on ctx output
Add a second-pass verification checklist
Limit ctx output to metadata, not recommendations
Review high-impact outputs before API calls
requires-engineering: implement validation rules between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. If those data classes are mixed in a shared workflow, retention, logging, or residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is stored in ctx logs or harness records
IF OpenBBTerminal outputs are retained under ctx logging policies
mitigations: Separate regulated and non-regulated datasets
Minimize logging of financial outputs
Review retention settings before running both agents
Delete shared artifacts after each run
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
